headline: Gold prices drop again in 2 days, falling by up to 2,158 BDT per bhori
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has reduced prices due to a decline in the global market, with silver prices also seeing a decrease.
details: Gold prices in Bangladesh have decreased for the second time in two days, with a maximum drop of 2,158 BDT per bhori. The new rates became effective from 10 AM on Monday.

headline: 415 detained in third phase of drive against teen gangs in Cumilla
summary: The district-wide operation, conducted across 18 police stations, follows the killing of a 13-year-old student.
details: Police detained 415 people in the third phase of a district-wide drive against teenage gangs in Cumilla. The operation was conducted simultaneously across all 18 police stations and by the District Detective Branch from 6:00pm yesterday to midnight.

The drive was led by Superintendent of Police Md Anisuzzaman and supervised by senior police officials. Detainees were picked up from various locations in Cumilla city and surrounding areas where police had received complaints about teenage troublemakers.
The detainees are currently being screened to determine their involvement in criminal activities, with legal action to be followed based on the findings.
In the first two phases of the campaign, police detained 624 and 254 people respectively. In the first phase, 451 were released after guardians furnished bonds, while 173 were sent to court.
In the second phase, 146 were released to guardians, while 108 were others were arrested in cases involving drug dealing, drug use, and activities related to banned organizations.
The heightened police activity comes after the killing of 13-year-old Ishayat Shahriar Oprotim, a class-seven student. Oprotim went missing on September 18 and his body was recovered on September 19.
Four people have already been arrested in connection with the killing of the student.
caption:
415 people detained in a single night. Cumilla police are cracking down on teen gangs.

Police detained 415 people in the third phase of a district-wide drive against teenage gangs in Cumilla. The operation was conducted simultaneously across all 18 police stations and by the District Detective Branch from 6:00pm yesterday to midnight.

The drive was led by Superintendent of Police Md Anisuzzaman and supervised by senior police officials. Detainees were picked up from various locations in Cumilla city and surrounding areas where police had received complaints about teenage troublemakers.

The detainees are currently being screened to determine their involvement in criminal activities, with legal action to be followed based on the findings.

In the first two phases of the campaign, police detained 624 and 254 people respectively. In the first phase, 451 were released after guardians furnished bonds, while 173 were sent to court.

In the second phase, 146 were released to guardians, while 108 were others were arrested in cases involving drug dealing, drug use, and activities related to banned organizations.

The heightened police activity comes after the killing of 13-year-old Ishayat Shahriar Oprotim, a class-seven student. Oprotim went missing on September 18 and his body was recovered on September 19.

Four people have already been arrested in connection with the killing of the student.
